title: Incremental isolation fallback router and smooth trip curves
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Problem: During cross-region capacity events we see large cohorts of requests that transiently push model backends to overload (long tail latency, queue pressure). Existing binary trip breakers are too coarse: they either allow the whole tenant through or cut them off, causing user-visible failures and noisy rollbacks. Goal: implement an incremental isolation + fallback router that applies smooth (non-binary) trip curves per dependency/model/tenant, isolates only the affected request cohorts, and redirects a fraction of traffic to safe fallbacks (cheaper model variant, cached response, read-only route) while preserving SLOs for the rest of the tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Router exposes per-path trip score (0.0-1.0) derived from sliding-window metrics (p99 latency, error rate, queue depth) and smoothing via EWMA
Traffic steering can route N% of matching requests to a fallback target where N is determined by the trip score (e.g., trip score 0.45 -> redirect 45% of eligible requests)
Fallback targets include: model-quantized variant, cached prefix lookup, and region-secondary endpoint; selection is policy-driven and configurable per tenant
SLO impact verified in canary: end-to-end user-facing p99 improves or stays within 10% while overall success rate remains >=SLO during injected overload tests
Operational metrics and dashboard updated: trip_score, redirected_rate, fallback_success_rate, rollback_count, per-tenant histograms
Fail-safe behaviour: if fallback target is unhealthy, router backs off and rebalancing attempt frequency is limited to avoid storming dependent services
tasks: Design trip_score calculation: inputs, decay window, weightings (latency, errors, queue), and calibration parameters
Implement incremental router module in serving-controlplane with pluggable fallback targets
Add policy DSL for tenant-level routing rules (percentile->fallback mapping) and default fallbacks
Integrate metrics emission for trip_score and redirected decisions into observability pipeline
Create integration tests that simulate region spike and verify smooth shedding curve semantics
Run customer-facing canary with two low-risk tenants and collect SLO and UX metrics
Document rollout steps and failure modes in runbook
decisions: Use EWMA on sliding windows (1m/5m) for smoothing rather than single-window thresholds to avoid oscillation
Percent-based redirection chosen over probabilistic hard-trips to allow gradual user experience degradation
Fallback preference order: cached response -> quantized model variant -> region-secondary endpoint
Trip score range normalized to 0.0-1.0 and mapped linearly to redirection percentage for initial rollout; later we may support nonlinear sigmoid mapping
tradeoffs: Smoother trip curves reduce noisy rollback but increase complexity and tuning surface for SREs
Redirecting to quantized models reduces cost and latency but can introduce quality regressions for corner prompts; mitigated with evaluation prompts in canary
Using EWMA adds latency to detection of very sharp failures; plan to include an emergency hard-trip path for extreme error spikes

review_feedback: PM (Rina Cho): Emphasize user-visible metrics in acceptance criteria and require UX sanity checks for redirected requests
Design (Elena Park): Add a flag in console to visualize per-tenant trip curve and allow manual pause of redirection
SRE (Jordan Lee): Ensure fallback selection avoids calling a fallback that shares the same overloaded dependency (dependency graph awareness)
Runtime (Samir Gupta): Prefer non-blocking checks in router path; use async health probes to keep tail latency low
testing_plan: Unit tests for score calculation with synthetic metric series
Integration test harness: inject p99 spikes and validate redirected_rate follows trip_score within 5%
Chaos test: saturate fallback target and assert router backoff prevents cascading failures
Canary: enable for 2 non-critical tenants for 48 hours and measure SLO delta and quality metrics on eval prompts
rollout_plan: Staged canary: two tenants for 48h, monitor dashboard and error budgets
Expand to 10 tenants with escalating thresholds over two weeks if metrics OK
Full platform enable with opt-out per tenant and console controls after 30 days
